rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph detains the brothers for three days, then keeps one while sending the others home for the youngest, telling them this will prove their innocence and preserve their lives amid famine.
rows.anchor: فقذفهم في الحبس ثلاثة أيام , ودعا بهم يوسف عليه الصلاة والسلام في اليوم الثالث , وقال لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers acknowledge they deserve their present affliction because they ignored Joseph's pleas and showed him no mercy.
rows.anchor: إنا قد استوجبنا السجن على أخينا إذ رأينا كرب نفسه إذا كان يتضرع إلينا فلم نرحمه

rows.speaker: روبيل
rows.claim: Reuben reminds them that he had warned them not to sin against the boy, and says they are now answerable for his blood.
rows.anchor: ألم أقل لكم : لا تأثموا بالغلام , فلم تقبلوا , وهو ذا الآن نحن مطالبون بدمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph understands the brothers through an interpreter; they do not know this, and he withdraws to weep before returning and detaining Simeon in their sight.
rows.anchor: ولم يعلموا أن يوسف يفهم كلامهم , لأنه أوقف ترجمانا بينه وبينهم , فتنحى عنهم فبكى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph provisions their journey and secretly returns each man's money to his sack.
rows.anchor: وأمر يوسف بملء أوعيتهم ميرة , وأمر برد ورق كل امرىء منهم في وعائه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When one brother finds his money at the top of his load, the brothers are terrified and wonder what God has done to them.
rows.anchor: فارتجفت قلوبهم وفزعت نفوسهم , وتعجب كل امرىء منهم , فقالوا : ياليت شعري ما هذا الذي صنعه الله بنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They tell Jacob that the Egyptian ruler called them spies; they claimed innocence and described their family, including the lost brother and youngest son still with their father.
rows.anchor: إن الرجل سيد الأرض كلمنا بفظاظة وقساوة . وحسبنا بمنزلة الجواسيس أتينا لنطالع الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They recount the ruler's condition that they return with their youngest brother, after which he would release their detained brother and let them trade.
rows.anchor: فأتوني بأخيكم الأصغر معكم , فأعلم حينئذ أنكم لستم بطلائع , بل أنتم أبرياء عدول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After finding every man's money in his sack, Jacob grieves that his sons have caused him to lose both Joseph and another son.
rows.anchor: فرأوا ورقهم مصروا ففزعوا هم وأبوهم . فقال لهم أبوهم : إنكم قد أثكلتموني ولدي وأفقدتموني إياهما

rows.speaker: روبيل
rows.claim: Reuben pledges that he will return Benjamin to Jacob, even wagering the loss of his own sons if he fails.
rows.anchor: ثكلت ابني جميعا إن لم آتك به ! ادفعه إلي وأنا أرده إلأيك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob refuses to send Benjamin because Joseph, presumed dead, was his only remaining son by that mother; he fears another mishap will make grief bring him to the grave.
rows.anchor: لا تهبط ابني معكم , لأن أخاه يوسف توفي وهو وحده الباقي لأمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the grain from Egypt is exhausted, Jacob again sends his sons to buy provisions.
rows.anchor: فاشتد الجوع على الأرض , ما أكلوا الذي أتوا به من مصر وأفنوه قال لهم يعقوب أبوهم عليه السلام

rows.speaker: يهوذا
rows.claim: Judah says the ruler warned them not to return unless their youngest brother came with them.
rows.anchor: إن الرجل أنذرنا وتقدم إلينا وقال : لا تعاينوا وجهي إلا وأخوكم معكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob asks why they told the ruler they had another brother; they answer that he had questioned them about their family and father.
rows.anchor: فقال لهم أبوهم : ولم أسأتم إلي فأخبرتم الرجل أن لكم أخا ؟ فقالوا : الرجل سأل عنا وعن رهطنا

rows.speaker: يهوذا
rows.claim: Judah asks Jacob to send the boy, guarantees his return, and accepts permanent blame before his father if he fails.
rows.anchor: سرح الغلام فننطلق فنحيى ولا نموت نحن وأنت أيضا وحشمنا , أنا أكفل به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob sends them with local produce, twice the money, and Benjamin, praying that God will gain them mercy and return both detained brothers.
rows.anchor: احملوا في أوعيتكم من ثمار هذه الأرض شيئا من صنوبر وعسل وعلك البطم وخروب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers arrive with Benjamin and a gift; Joseph directs that they be brought into his house and that a meal be prepared.
rows.anchor: فأخذ القوم هذه الهدية وضعفا من الفضة , وانطلقوا معهم ببنيامين وأتوا يوسف فوقفوا بين يديه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They fear they are being taken in over the returned money and will be enslaved, with their animals seized.
rows.anchor: إنهم إنما يدخلوننا لسبب الورق الذي وجدنا في أعدالنا من قبل , فيريدون أن يتطاولوا علينا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph's steward reassures the brothers that their God returned their money and brings Simeon out to them.
rows.anchor: إلهكم إله المواعيد إله أبيكم ذخر لكم هذه الذخيرة في أوعيتكم , لأن ورقكم قد صار في قبضتي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers present their gift and prostrate; Joseph asks after their father, recognizes Benjamin, prays for God's tenderness toward him, and withdraws to weep before composing himself.
rows.anchor: فأبصر بنيامين أخاه ابن أمه فقال لهم : هذا أخوكم الذي أخبرتموني عنه ؟

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Egyptians consider eating with Hebrews impure, so Joseph has the meal served separately and seats the brothers by age.
rows.anchor: لأنه لا يستطيع أهل مصر أن يأكلوا مع العبرانيين , لأن هذه نجاسة عند المصريين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph gives Benjamin five portions, more than any of his brothers.
rows.anchor: فأعطى كل واحد منهم من بين يديه جزءا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph orders his silver cup placed with Benjamin's money, then sends his steward to accuse the brothers of stealing the cup used for drinking and divination.
rows.anchor: وخذ طاسي طاس الفضة وصيره في وعاء الأصغر مع ورق ميرته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers deny stealing and offer death for the one found with the cup and slavery for themselves; the search finds it in Benjamin's sack, and they rend their clothes.
rows.anchor: فوجدوا الطاس في وعاء بنيامين , فمزقوا ثيابهم وخرقوها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Judah and the brothers offer themselves as slaves, citing Jacob's grief and Judah's guarantee to return Benjamin; Judah offers to remain in the boy's place.
rows.anchor: لأن عبدك ضمن الغلام لأبينا , وقلت : إني إذا لم آتك به أخطىء باقي جميع الأيام

rows.speaker: يوسف
rows.claim: Joseph refuses to enslave them all: only the one found with the cup will remain his servant, while the others may return safely to their father.
rows.anchor: معاذ الله أن أفعل هذا ! بل الرجل الذي وجد الكأس عنده يكون لي عبدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers' intense despair follows Joseph's steady refusal to release Benjamin, despite his prior kindness, tenderness, and mercy toward them.
rows.anchor: تحول رجاءهم لتخلية سبيله لما رأوا من إحسانه ولطفه ورحمته يأسا شديدا

rows.speaker: الرماني
rows.claim: In “خلصوا نجيا,” they separated from others for private counsel; “نجيا” relates to secret consultation and can derive from rising above the ground.
rows.anchor:
من المناجاة وهي رفع المعنى من كل واحد إلى صاحبه في خفاء , من النجو وهو الارتفاع عن الأرض -
قاله الرماني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, “نجيا” portrays them as wholly absorbed in confidential deliberation, as though they themselves embodied the consultation.
rows.anchor: أو تمحضوا تناجيا لإفاضتم فيه بجد كأنهم صورة التناجي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their eldest brother is Reuben; he reminds them of Jacob's divine pledge so they will work hard to avoid their father's anger.
rows.anchor: قال كبيرهم } في السن وهو روبيل : { ألم تعلموا } مقرا لهم بما يعرفونه مع قرب الزمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “A pledge from God” describes Jacob's oath as divinely instituted, binding them to return Benjamin unless they were overwhelmed by an unavoidable calamity.
rows.anchor: ولما كان الله تعالى هو الذي شرعه - كما مضى - كان كأنه منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reuben recalls their earlier grave failure regarding Joseph; the emphatic “ما” leaves no doubt that they were negligent, so Jacob will not believe them.
rows.anchor: في } ضياع { يوسف } فلا يصدقكم أبوكم أصلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The basic sense of tafrīṭ is to go ahead, as in the Prophet's saying, “I precede you at the Basin.”
rows.anchor: وأصل معنى التفريط , : التقدم , من قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( أنا فرطكم على الحوض )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “I will not leave this land” uses the verb without a preposition, signaling the eldest brother's strong attachment to remaining there.
rows.anchor: فلن أبرح } أي أفارق هذه { الأرض } بسبب هذا , وإيصاله الفعل بدون حرف دليل على أنه صار شديد الالتصاق بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He will remain until his father permits departure or God rules for him, by freeing his brother or enabling some other way out; God is the best judge because knowledge and power realize the best outcome.
rows.anchor: حتى يأذن لي أبي } في الذهاب منها { أو يحكم الله } أي الذي له الكمال كله ووثقنا به { لي } بخلاص أخي أو بالذهاب منها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The eldest brother sends the others back so Jacob may come to Egypt or devise another way to resolve the crisis; he tells them to speak to their father gently.
rows.anchor: أمرهم بالرجوع ليعلموا أباهم لإمكان أن يريد القدوم إلى مصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Your son stole” identifies Benjamin, Joseph's full brother, whom Jacob regards as the most complete of them in prophethood.
rows.anchor: إن ابنك } أي شقيق يوسف عليه الصلاة والسلام الذي هو أكملنا في النبوة عندك { سرق }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers say they testified only to what they saw—the cup coming from Benjamin's bag; testimony ordinarily reports perceived acts or words, but may also rest on decisive proof.
rows.anchor: والشهادة : الخبر عن إحساس قول أو فعل , وتجوز الشهادة بما أدى إليه الدليل القطعي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their claim not to guard the unseen leaves open that a scheme they did not know about produced the apparent theft, as with their returned money.
rows.anchor: فلعل حيلة دبرت في ذلك غاب عنا علمها كما صنع في رد بضاعتنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The “village” is Egypt, whose people—and even walls, if they spoke—could confirm the story; the brothers also appeal to the Canaanite caravan they traveled with.
rows.anchor: وهي مصر , عما أخبرناك به يخبروك بصدقنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author explains “qarya” as a bounded settlement, from gathering water, and “ʿīr” as a caravan of donkeys, later generalized to other caravans.
rows.anchor: والقرية : الأرض الجامعة لحدود فاصلة , وأصلها من قريت الماء , أي جمعته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They emphasize truthfulness because Benjamin's generous brotherly character makes the apparent theft surprising.
rows.anchor: ولما كان ذلك جديرا بالإنكار لما يتحقق من كرم أخيهم , أكدوه بقولهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob rejects the charge: Benjamin neither stole the cup nor intended to; Joseph and his herald do not directly attribute theft to him, and the brothers' earlier treatment of Joseph caused this crisis.
rows.anchor: لأن بنيامين لم يسرق الصواع ولا هم بذلك , ولذلك لم ينسبه يوسف عليه الصلاة والسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob's “beautiful patience” rests on his good expectation of God; his intuition is that Joseph's actions caused the crisis and that Joseph, Benjamin, and Reuben will reunite with him.
rows.anchor: ما يدل الفطن على أنه تفرس أن هذه الأفعال نشأت عن يوسف عليه الصاة والسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is “knowing, wise”: He knows the hidden causes that lead to the goal and orders them so well that no one can undo His arrangement; knowledge is especially needed amid uncertainty.
rows.anchor: لأن الحال داع إلى العلم بما غاب من الاسباب أكثر من دعائه إلى معرفة حكمتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob turns away in overwhelming grief and addresses his complaint to God alone; “yā asafā” is an address to his deepest sorrow, with final alif replacing the possessive yāʾ to signal its boundlessness.
rows.anchor: { وقال } مشتكيا إلى الله لا غيره , فهو تعريض بأشد التصريح والدعاء : { ياأسفي }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The natural, unintentional sound-play between asaf (grief) and Yūsuf marks rhetorical artistry; Joseph is singled out as the source from which later griefs branched.
rows.anchor: وجناس ( الأسف ) مع ( يوسف ) مما لم يتعمدن فيكون مطبوعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeated weeping turns Jacob's eyes white and blinds him; his grief is likened to that of seventy bereaved women, yet he never mistrusts God's promise.
rows.anchor: أي انقلب سوادهما إلى حال البياض كثرة الاستعبار , فعمى البصر { من الحزن }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Kazīm” means filled with distress yet restraining its expression; its passive intensive form is stronger than “makẓūm,” and Jacob's self-control reflects his knowledge and wisdom.
rows.anchor: شديد الكظم لامتلائه من الكرب , مانع نفسه من عمل ما يقتضيه ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root k-ẓ-m centers on preventing expression: its derivatives describe swallowed anger, a filled and sealed waterskin, a camel holding back its cud, breath, restraints, and channels that contain water.
rows.anchor: ومادة ( كظم ) تدور على المنع من الإظهار , يلزمه الكرب - لأنه من شأن الممنوع مما قد امتلأ منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers swear by God in astonishment and say Jacob will not cease mentioning Joseph until he is wasted and mentally broken or dies; the explanation recalls “rouse the believers to fight.”
rows.anchor: { تالله } أي الملك الأعظم , يمينا فيها تعجب { تفتئوا } أي ما تزال { تذكر يوسف }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob says continued remembrance is a human virtue of tenderness and loyalty; it is blameworthy only when one complains to creatures, whereas he complains to God alone.
rows.anchor: لأنه من صفات الكمال للإنسان , لدلالته على الرقة والوفاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Bathth” is grief so difficult to bear that one discloses it; “ḥuzn” is broader sorrow, even when its cause is light enough for people to relieve.
rows.anchor: والبث أشد الحزن , سمي بذلك لأنه من صعوبته لا يطاق حمله فيباح به وينشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob knows God's kindness to his household and His relief of the distressed; he believes Joseph remains alive and expects God to reunite them, unlike his sons.
rows.anchor: يغلب على ظنه أن يوسف عليه السلام حي ويظن في الله أن يجمع شمله به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author gives a lexicon of the roots and forms related to “فتأ,” associating them with youth, strength, and firm resolve; the next segments continue its detailed forms.
rows.anchor: ومادة ( فتا ) يائية وواوية مهموزة وغير ومهموزة بكل ترتيب وهي فتأ

rows.speaker: عن ابن مالك
rows.claim: With al-Farrāʾ's attribution and al-Qāmūs's endorsement, “ما فتئ” means “continues”; in this construction “فتئ” is restricted to occur after a preceding negation.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن مالك في جمع اللغات المشكلة وعزاه للفراء - وصححه في القاموسك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root's derivatives connect “ما فتأ يفعل” (he does not cease) to a youth's vigorous, decisive, unyielding action; “ما فتىء” can mean he promptly undertook it.
rows.anchor: ما فتأ يفعل كذا - مثلثة العين : ما زال كما أفتا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Related forms name a youth, generous or brave young man, servant, pupil, and generosity; “أفتاه” means to explain a matter and “فتوى” is a jurist's answer.
rows.anchor: والفتى - بالقصر ؛ السخي والكريم , أي الجواد الشريف النفس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other derivatives express sudden death, outstripping someone, separation, difference or defect, and acting ahead of another's authority; these meanings retain the sense of force or surpassing.
rows.anchor: ومن واوية : فات الشيء فوتا وفواتا : ذهب فسبق فلم يدرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Further derivatives describe “iftāt” as ruling or deciding by force, alongside words connected to strength, speed, anger, and timing.
rows.anchor: ابتدعه - كما تقدم في المهموز , وافتات عليه : حكم - لقوته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob orders his sons to search with all their senses and effort for Joseph and Benjamin, which supports the earlier inference that he suspects Joseph arranged events.
rows.anchor: فتحسسوا } أي بجميع جهدكم { من يوسف وأخيه } أي اطلبوا من أخبارهم بحواسكم

rows.speaker: الرماني
rows.claim: Al-Rummānī derives “rūḥ” from a pleasant, comforting breeze; here it means God's mercy, relief, ease, and gentle care in restoring what is scattered.
rows.anchor: والروح - قال الرماني - يقع بريح تلذ , وكأن هذا أصله فالمراد : من رحمته وفرجه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only disbelievers despair of God's relief because they reject the source of hope and lack the faith and resolve to seek it.
rows.anchor: إنه لا يبأس } أي لا يقنط { من روح الله } أي الذي له جميع صفات الجلال والإكرام { إلا القوم } أي الذين لهم قوة المحاولة { الكافرون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers quickly return to Egypt for grain; the opening “fa-lammā” signals their haste, and “yā ayyuhā al-ʿazīz” respectfully alerts the ruler to their grave need.
rows.anchor: فأجابوه إلى ما أراد , قتوجهوا إلى مصر لذلك ولقصد الميرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They admit that famine has afflicted them and their family and offer paltry, undesirable merchandise; they ask for full measure and additional charity because they are weak and needy.
rows.anchor: مسنا } أي أيتها العصابة التي تراها { وأهلنا } أي الذين تركناهم في بلادنا { الضر } أي لابسنا ملابسة نحسها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They appeal to God's reward for charitable giving, even when the recipient appears wealthy, and especially when the needy are weak.
rows.anchor: يجزي المتصدقين * } أي مطلقا وإن أظهرت - بما أفاد الإظهار - وإن كانت على غنى قوي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Joseph story teaches patience, measured action, and entrusting matters to the Wise; difficult affairs unfold gradually as causes are ordered, testing both obedience and disobedience.
rows.anchor: على الاقتداء بأفعال الهداة المهديين في التأني والاتئاد وتفويض الأمور إلى الحكيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers confess God preferred Joseph over them through knowledge, intellect, judgment, beauty, rule, piety, and other virtues; the shortened “in” heightens their urgent apology.
rows.anchor: فضلك علينا أي بالعلم والعقل والحكم والحسن والملك والتقوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They call themselves intrinsically wrongdoers; “khaṭiʾīn” denotes deliberately committing sin.
rows.anchor: أي عريقين في الخطأ , وهو تعمد الإثم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph's “no reproach today” removes blame precisely when blame seems warranted, so there is all the more reason for no reproach later.
rows.anchor: وإن كان هذا الوقت مظنة اللوم والتأنيب , فإذا انتفى ذلك فيه فما الظن بما بعده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Tathrīb” means reproaching someone by stripping away the covering of pardon; the root's associations include persistence, confinement, and destruction, its dominant tendency being ruin.
rows.anchor: والتثريب : التقرير بالذنب , فهو إزالة ما على الإنسان من ساتر العفو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph prays that God forgive all their past and possible future lapses; the imperfect verb encourages sincere repentance and hope in the Most Merciful, especially for the penitent.
rows.anchor: ولعله عبر في هذا الدعاء بالمضارع إرشادا لهم إلى إخلاص التوبة , ورغبهم في ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers reportedly felt embarrassed accepting Joseph's daily hospitality; he says Egyptian observers once saw him as a slave bought for twenty dirhams, but now esteem him because he is their brother and Abraham's descendant.
rows.anchor: روى أنهم أرسلوا إليه أنك لتدعونا إلى طعامك وكرامتك بكرة وعشيا ونحن نستحي

rows.speaker: الرماني
rows.claim: Al-Rummānī defines “ḍalāl” here as moving away from the right direction.
rows.anchor: قال الرماني : و الضلال : الذهاب عن جهة الصواب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The bearer is Judah with Joseph's shirt; the added “an” and the sequencing of “when” convey that he arrived and immediately cast it on Jacob's face, restoring sight at once.
rows.anchor: جاء البشير } وهو يهوذا بذلك , معه القميص { ألقاه } أي القميص حين وصل إلى يعقوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob's restored sight verifies his claim that he knew from God what his sons did not, including Joseph's news and other divine gifts.
rows.anchor: فصحح الله قوله وحقق وجدانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sons ask Jacob to seek forgiveness for their sins; each pronoun plainly refers to its owner, so the text need not repeat the subject.
rows.anchor: ورد كل ضمير من هذه الضمائر إلى صاحبه في غاية الوضوح

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: Jacob's sons confess intentional wrongdoing against Joseph; the author cites a Prophetic report that when a servant confesses sin and repents, God accepts the repentance.
rows.anchor: كما قال صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( إن العبد إذا اعترف بذنبه ثم تاب تاب الله عليه )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob promises to ask his Lord for forgiveness, invoking the Lord who has always nurtured him well, to reassure his sons and strengthen their hope.
rows.anchor: لكم ربي } أي الذي لم يزل يحسن إلي ويربيني أحسن تربية , فهو الجدير بأن يغفر لبني

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Reported explanations for “sawfa” say Jacob delayed his prayer until the night prayer or Friday night; another says asking the young is easier than asking the elderly.
rows.anchor: وقيل : لأنه أخر الدعاء إلى صلاة الليل , وقيل : إلى ليلة الجمعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The family arrives in Egypt as seventy-two males and females, apparently making haste; Joseph receives them among Egypt's people and establishes his encampment for them.
rows.anchor: ثم قدموا مصر وهم اثنان وسبعون نفسا من الذكور والإناث

rows.speaker: الحسن وابن إسحاق
rows.claim: Al-Hasan and Ibn Isḥāq, as cited by al-Rummānī and Abū Ḥayyān, say Joseph's mother was his actual mother; the author says this is the apparent reading.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أنها أمه حقيقة , وبه قال الحسن وابن إسحاق - كما نقله الرماني وأبو حيان

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the woman called Joseph's mother was his maternal aunt.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما أنها خالته

rows.speaker: الرماني
rows.claim: Al-Rummānī explains that the condition “if God wills” qualifies their being safe, not their entering Egypt; Joseph promises safety from all misfortunes.
rows.anchor: وأتى بالشرط للأمن لا للدخول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After they settle, Joseph raises his parents onto the elevated throne; “ʿarsh” derives from elevation, according to al-Rummānī.
rows.anchor: على العرش } أي السرير الرفيع ؛ قال الرماني : أصله الرفع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The parents and brothers prostrate to Joseph, fulfilling his dream; prostration then meant submission and humility and was permitted in that age.
rows.anchor: وخروا } أي انحطوا { له سجدا } الأبوان والإخوة تحقيقا لرؤياه ممن هو غالب على كل أمر , والسجود - وأصله : الخضوع والتذلل - كان مباحا في تلك الأزمنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph tenderly addresses Jacob as father and calls the prostration the interpretation of his earlier dream; “taʾwīl” is explanation in light of the speech's eventual outcome.
rows.anchor: هذا } أي الذي وقع من السجود { تأويل رؤياي } التي رأيتها

rows.speaker: سلمان
rows.claim: Salman reports that forty years passed between Joseph's dream and its interpretation.
rows.anchor: وعن سلمان رضي الله عنه أن ما بين تأويلها رؤياها أربعون سنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph says God showed kindness “to” him, a preposition suggesting greater closeness than “toward”; he says “prison” instead of “pit” to avoid upsetting his brothers.
rows.anchor: وتعدية { أحسن } بالباء أدل على القرب من المحسن من التعدية ب ( إلى )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His family came from the outskirts of Palestine's desert; they were nomadic herders who moved among pastures, so their arrival was a great blessing.
rows.anchor: من أطراف بادية فلسطين , وذلك من أكبر النعم

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The author invokes a Prophetic saying that God moves to settled life the person for whom He wills good, illustrating the blessing of coming from the desert.
rows.anchor: كما ورد في الحديث ( من يرد الله به خيرا ينقله من البادية إلى الحاضرة )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “After Satan stirred up” uses past tense to show the discord had ended; Joseph says the stirring was between him and his brothers without singling out blame, fulfilling Jacob's prediction.
rows.anchor: عبر بالماضي ليفهم أنه انقضى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Remembering God's gifts of rule and knowledge, Joseph turns away from worldly attachment and prays to his Lord, introducing the prayer with “قد” because the audience awaits the dream's outcome.
rows.anchor: وافتتح ب ( قد ) لأن الحال حال توقع السامع لشرح مآل الرؤيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph modestly says God gave him only part of kingship and taught him part of interpretation; this fulfills his father's prediction and God's earlier promise of authority.
rows.anchor: وقصر دعواه تواضعا بالإتيان بالجار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling God Creator of the heavens and earth gathers the divine attributes of knowledge and wisdom; Joseph says God alone is his inward and outward protector in both lives.
rows.anchor: ثم ناداه بوصف جامع للعلم والحكمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A true protector acts for his beloved's best, so Joseph asks God to give him an even greater good in the afterlife than He gave him in this world.
rows.anchor: والولي يفعل لمولاه الأصلح والأحسن , فأحسن بي في الآخرة أعظم ما أحسنت بي في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph asks to die wholly and completely Muslim; he clarifies genuine submission as deep sincerity by asking to be joined with the righteous.
rows.anchor: { توفني } أي اقبض روحي وافيا تاما في جميع أمري حسا ومعنى حال كوني { مسلما }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God grants Joseph's request; Egyptians reportedly dispute where to bury him to share his blessing, then bury a marble coffin in the Nile so its water benefits all the land equally.
rows.anchor: وتخاصم أهل مصر فيه , كلهم يرجوا أن يدفن في محلته يرجو بركته

rows.speaker: التوراة
rows.claim: In the Torah account, Joseph dismisses the attendants, weeps aloud, identifies himself to his frightened brothers, assures them that God sent him ahead to preserve them through the famine, and tells them to bring Jacob to Egypt.
rows.anchor: ذكر ما بقي من القصة عن التوراة : قال بعدما مضى : فلم يقدر يوسف على الصبر

rows.speaker: التوراة
rows.claim: Joseph invites Jacob and the family to Goshen and promises to feed them through five remaining famine years; he has Benjamin witness their conversation and embraces and weeps with his brothers.
rows.anchor: فكن قريبا مني أنت وبنوك وأهل بيتك وعمتك وبقرك وجمع مالك , فأمونكم هناك , لأنه قد بقي خمس سنين جوعا

rows.speaker: التوراة
rows.claim: Pharaoh rejoices at Joseph's brothers' arrival, offers Egypt's best land, directs them to bring Jacob and their households, and supplies travel provisions, garments, and special gifts for Benjamin and their father.
rows.anchor: فقال فرعون ليوسف : قل لإخوتك فليفعلوا هكذا , أوقروا دوابكم ميرة

rows.speaker: التوراة
rows.claim: Joseph warns his brothers not to quarrel on the road; they reach Canaan and tell Jacob that Joseph is alive, prompting Jacob to set out to see him before he dies.
rows.anchor: وتقدم لهم : لا تقع المشاجرة فيما بينكم في الطريق

rows.speaker: التوراة
rows.claim: At Beer-sheba, Jacob offers a sacrifice; God appears to him in a night vision, tells him not to fear Egypt, promises to make him a great nation, go down and return with him, and says Joseph will close his eyes at death.
rows.anchor: فكلم الله إسرائيل في الرؤيا وقال له : يا يعقوب ! فقال : هأنذا ! فقال : إني أنا إيل إله أبيك , لا تخف من الحدور إلى مصر

rows.speaker: التوراة
rows.claim: Jacob and all his descendants enter Egypt, and the Torah account proceeds to enumerate them.
rows.anchor: وأدخل إلى مصر كل نسله , ثم سماهم واحدا

rows.speaker: التوراة
rows.claim: Joseph plans to tell Pharaoh his family are shepherds and asks them to say their occupation has always been herding, since Egyptians despise shepherds and this will secure their settlement in Goshen.
rows.anchor: والقوم رعاء غنم , لأنهم أصحاب مواش وقد أتوا بغنمهم وبقرهم وبكل شيء لهم

rows.speaker: التوراة
rows.claim: Pharaoh questions five brothers, accepts their request for Goshen because famine has stripped Canaan of pasture, and offers them the best land; Joseph brings Jacob, who says he is 130 and blesses Pharaoh.
rows.anchor: مبلغ حياتي مائة وثلاثون سنة , وإن أيام حياتي الناقصة

rows.speaker: التوراة
rows.claim: Joseph settles the family in fertile Rameses (also identified as Ain Shams) and rations grain by household size; during the severe famine he collects Egyptian and Canaanite money into Pharaoh's treasury and then exchanges grain for livestock.
rows.anchor: فأسكن يوسف عليه السلام أباه يعقوب عليه السلام وإخوته وأعكاهم وراثة في أرض مصر في أخصب الأرض

rows.speaker: التوراة
rows.claim: The Torah account counts seventy descendants of Jacob entering Egypt.
rows.anchor: فجميع بني يعقوب الذين ادخلوا مصر سبعون إنسانا

rows.speaker: التوراة
rows.claim: Joseph buys all Egyptian land for Pharaoh except the priests' land, moves the people among cities, gives seed, and sets a permanent one-fifth crop tax while households retain four-fifths; priests are exempt because Pharaoh maintains them.
rows.anchor: فاتباع يوسف لفرعون جميع أرض مصرن فصارت الأرض لفرعونن فنقل الشعب

rows.speaker: التوراة
rows.claim: The Egyptians thank Joseph for saving their lives and accept permanent service to Pharaoh under his arrangement; Israel prospers in Goshen.
rows.anchor: لقد أحييتنا , فلنظفر من سيدنا برحمة ورأفة , ونكون عبيدا لفرعون

rows.speaker: التوراة
rows.claim: Jacob lives in Egypt for seventeen years, dies at 147, and asks Joseph to swear not to bury him there but to carry him to the burial place of his ancestors; Joseph swears and Jacob worships leaning on his staff.
rows.anchor: وعاش يعقوب في أرض مصر سبع عشرة سنة , وكانت جميع أيام حياة يعقوب مائة وسبعا أربعين سنة
